scams.name: Manaus (MAO) Airport Taxi & Late-Night Transfer Overcharge
scams.description:
Manaus International Airport (Aeroporto Eduardo Gomes, IATA MAO) sits 14 km north of Centro Histórico and 11 km north of Ponta Negra (the main tourist district). Limited late-night rideshare supply plus predatory 'Special Taxi' kiosks create a systematic overcharge pattern that catches tourists unfamiliar with legitimate Uber pricing.

Legitimate cost in 2026: Uber/99 from MAO to Ponta Negra R$45–R$75 (30 min); to Centro Histórico R$35–R$60 (25 min); to Tropical Manaus Ecoresort R$50–R$80 (30 min). Budget public option: the Executivo MAO-Centro bus is R$17.30 per person (60 min to Centro), runs 5 AM–11 PM. The 2025 scam patterns: 'Special Taxi' kiosks inside MAO terminal quote R$150–R$280 flat to Ponta Negra; curbside touts at arrivals offer 'only R$180 to your hotel, meter broken'; late-night (after 11 PM) Uber wait times spike to 20–35 min because of low rideshare supply in northern Amazonas, with unlicensed mototaxistas filling the gap; Uber/99 drivers occasionally demand cash top-up R$50–R$100 after pickup; 'city-tour transfer' upsells at arrivals at R$300; some hotels add 30–50% mark-up on pre-booked transfers; and unlicensed mototáxis at arrivals offer R$40 fixed but pose documented 2024–2025 robbery risk.

For travelers, the practical defense lives at the official Aplicativos pickup zone. Book Uber or 99 on airport Wi-Fi after collecting luggage — meet your driver at the official 'Aplicativos' pickup zone at Terminal 2 arrivals (signposted) — and ignore every 'Special Taxi' kiosk inside the terminal quoting R$150+, since those are the overcharge operation. For late-night arrivals (after 11 PM), pre-book a transfer via your hotel or Amazon Tours Transfer at R$120–R$180 fixed — worth it to avoid app-wait frustration in an unfamiliar city. Don't use an unlicensed mototaxi with luggage or after dark — Manaus has documented 2024–2025 mototaxi-robbery incidents. For return to MAO, pre-book Uber the night before. If your Uber driver demands cash top-up, refuse politely, cancel in-app, and rebook; use the in-app safety button if pressure escalates. Decline hotel 'transfer service' at 30–50% mark-up — book Uber directly from the lobby. DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373 (Polícia Turística Amazonas); Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192.
scams.avoidance: Uber / 99 from MAO to Ponta Negra R$45–R$75; to Centro R$35–R$60 Late-night: pre-book Amazon Tours Transfer / hotel transfer R$120–R$180 fixed NEVER use unlicensed mototaxi with luggage / after dark (robbery-incident pattern) Meet driver at 'Aplicativos' pickup zone Terminal 2 — ignore Special Taxi kiosks DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190
scams.location: Aeroporto Eduardo Gomes (MAO), arrivals hall, curbside
scams.tldr: Manaus Airport (MAO) 'Special Taxi' kiosks quote R$150–R$280 flat to Ponta Negra (real Uber R$45–R$75) and curbside touts run 'meter broken R$180' offers — late-night rideshare supply collapses after 11 PM, where unlicensed mototaxis fill the gap with documented robbery risk.

scams.name: Amazon Jungle Lodge Booking Fraud & Commission-Stop Day-Trip Scam
scams.description:
The Amazon jungle lodge and river-cruise industry around Manaus has a documented commission-markup and booking-fraud ecosystem, and is the most common tourist complaint against the city. The structural vulnerability: legitimate operators have spotty online presence (Marinha do Brasil registration, FUNAI compliance, real Tripadvisor reviews are real signals but not always findable in 5 minutes), while clone operators on Instagram and WhatsApp are perfectly polished and demand PIX-irreversible deposits.

Legitimate 2026 cost ranges: 3-day / 2-night Amazon jungle lodge (all-inclusive — transfer, lodge, meals, 3 daily activities) is R$1,800–R$3,500 per person via reputable operators (Juma Amazon Lodge, Anavilhanas Jungle Lodge, Uacari Lodge, Amazon Eco Park Lodge, Tariri Amazon Lodge). 4–5-day trips R$3,000–R$6,000 per person. Day-trip Encontro das Águas + piranha fishing + Amazônia village R$250–R$400 per person (group, 8–10 hours). Private 2-person Encontro das Águas speedboat R$1,200–R$1,800 total. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) airport tour-desk / hotel lobby selling 'exclusive 3-night lodge package R$8,500 per person' with commission markup 2–3x real rate; (b) WhatsApp + Instagram 'operator' demanding PIX deposit for a lodge that doesn't exist — classic Brazilian PIX-irreversible fraud; (c) day-trip 'Encontro das Águas + tour' that becomes 3 commission stops (artisanal market, 'traditional village' for R$100 entry, a 'pink-dolphin swim' with captive animals R$200 upsell) with little actual Encontro time; (d) unlicensed 'jungle guide' offering 'authentic off-grid R$500 per day' without insurance, radio, or Marinha registration — documented 2024 fatalities; (e) fake 'eco-lodge' operators on booking.com with cloned reviews from legitimate lodges — verify lodge NAME on Marinha do Brasil registered-vessel list; (f) 'pink-dolphin feeding village' attraction — animal-welfare prohibited since 2025; operators still selling to unaware tourists; (g) 'wild Amazon tribe visit R$600' — indigenous-contact tourism is FUNAI-regulated and requires permits; most 'tribe visits' are staged performances in commercialized Amazônia villages; (h) lodge 'surprise extras' on checkout — additional R$400–R$800 for 'generator fuel' / 'kitchen staff tip' / 'cleaning fee' not disclosed on booking.

For travelers, the practical defense lives in the booking channel and the payment method. Book direct with recognized Amazon lodges via their official websites — Juma Amazon Lodge (jumalodge.com), Anavilhanas Jungle Lodge (anavilhanaslodge.com), Uacari Lodge (uacari.com), Amazon Eco Park Lodge, and Tariri Amazon Lodge — all with verified Marinha registration plus FUNAI compliance, and pay via credit card only (never PIX) since card chargebacks give you recourse and PIX doesn't. Read Tripadvisor and Google reviews for the lodge name and cross-check recent 2024–2025 reviews mentioning specific operational details (room amenities, exact itinerary, named guides) rather than generic 'amazing experience' 5-star copy-paste. Avoid every 'hotel lobby R$8,500 exclusive package' upsell — commission markup is 2–3×. For day-trips, book through your hotel's partnered operator (Gero Tours, Viverde, Amazonastur) at R$250–R$400 group rate. Refuse every 'pink-dolphin feeding' or 'wild tribe visit' — both violate animal-welfare or FUNAI regulation; reputable lodges do not offer these. For travelers, 3-night at one reputable lodge (Juma, Anavilhanas, or Amazon Eco Park) is the gold-standard experience. Confirm the lodge's Marinha do Brasil boat registration before booking; legitimate operators share the vessel number on request. AMAZONASTUR (state tourism board) +55 92 2123 8800 for operator verification; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: Book DIRECT via official lodge websites: Juma / Anavilhanas / Uacari / Amazon Eco Park / Tariri Verify Marinha registration + FUNAI compliance + 2024–2025 specific Tripadvisor reviews Use CREDIT CARD only (not PIX) for deposit — enables chargeback recourse Day-trips: book via hotel-partnered Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur R$250–R$400 group AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800 to verify any operator; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Manaus hotel lobbies, airport tour-desks, online travel sites, Ponta Negra tour-office strip
scams.tldr: Manaus Amazon jungle lodge bookings face PIX-irreversible WhatsApp/Instagram fraud, hotel-lobby 'exclusive R$8,500 packages' at 2–3× real lodge rates, and day-trips that become 3 commission-stop circuits — Juma, Anavilhanas, Uacari, Amazon Eco Park, and Tariri are the verified-Marinha-registered lodges to book direct.

scams.name: Encontro das Águas Boat-Tour Overcharge & Unlicensed-Operator Safety Risk
scams.description:
Encontro das Águas (Meeting of the Waters), where the black Rio Negro meets the café-au-lait Rio Solimões to form the Amazon proper 10 km downstream of Manaus, is the flagship half-day or full-day boat excursion — and hosts a parallel overcharge plus unlicensed-operator safety risk pattern. The Amazonas river itself has documented capsize and engine-failure risk in the confluence zone, which makes the unlicensed-boat variant materially more dangerous than the parallel scam in calmer waters elsewhere.

Legitimate 2026 cost: full-day Encontro das Águas + Janauari Ecological Park (mangroves, piranha fishing, village visit, lunch) via Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur group boat R$250–R$400 per person (8 hours, includes lunch + 30–50 pax boat). Private small-group speedboat for 2–4 passengers R$1,200–R$1,800 total. The Encontro das Águas confluence itself is a 60–90 minute stop; most of the day is transit + Janauari Park activities. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Porto de Manaus tout selling 'VIP private speedboat Encontro R$2,500' to a single couple (real private 2-pax R$1,200–R$1,800); (b) 'helicopter Encontro tour R$4,500 per person' (real boat R$250–R$400 is sufficient — the confluence visual is at water level not air); (c) unlicensed speedboats at Ponta Negra pier offering R$800 private — no life jackets, no Marinha registration, no radio, no insurance; Amazonas river has documented capsize + engine-failure risk; (d) 'pink dolphin swim R$300 extra' upsell — animal-welfare prohibited since 2025 per IBAMA decree; reputable operators do NOT offer this; (e) 'mandatory environmental tax R$150' demanded at Janauari Park entrance (real R$25 Parque Estadual do Rio Negro entry); (f) 'lunch R$250 mandatory' on the boat (real: reputable group-tour price R$250–R$400 INCLUDES lunch — don't pay extra); (g) unlicensed boat operator 'piranha fishing R$100 extra' (standard group tour includes piranha fishing + bait); (h) Centro Histórico tout selling 'speedboat direct from the port R$400 without tour stops' — these are unregulated transfers that may skip Janauari and return in 3 hours vs the advertised 8.

For travelers, the practical defense lives at the boarding pier with two safety checks. Book the group tour via your hotel's partnered operator (Gero Tours, Viverde, or Amazonastur) at R$250–R$400 per person — and verify the boat's Marinha do Brasil registration sticker plus working life jackets for every passenger before boarding, refusing to board any vessel that lacks either. Confirm the itinerary in writing (departure time, Encontro stop duration, Janauari activities, lunch, return time). Refuse every 'helicopter Encontro tour' upsell — the confluence is visually best at water level; helicopter at 2,000m misses the color contrast. Refuse every 'pink-dolphin swim' offer (illegal per 2025 IBAMA decree). Refuse 'mandatory environmental tax R$150' — real Janauari Park entry is R$25. For photos, sit on the left side of the boat on the outbound leg (Rio Negro is on your left facing downstream). Dramamine 30 min before boarding — Amazonas currents can be rough at the confluence line. AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: Book group tour via Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur R$250–R$400 per person VERIFY Marinha registration sticker BEFORE boarding; CHECK life jackets for every passenger REFUSE pink-dolphin swim (illegal IBAMA 2025) + helicopter upsell + 'mandatory R$150 tax' CONFIRM itinerary in writing: Encontro duration, Janauari activities, lunch, return time Dramamine 30 min pre-board; AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800; DEATUR +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Porto de Manaus + Ponta Negra pier + Marina David
scams.tldr: Encontro das Águas group boat tours run R$250–R$400 via Gero Tours/Viverde/Amazonastur (8 hours including Janauari Park + lunch) — but Porto de Manaus touts sell 'VIP private R$2,500' for 2 people and unlicensed speedboats at Ponta Negra pier offer R$800 with no life jackets, no Marinha registration, no radio, no insurance.

scams.name: Centro Histórico & Mercado Adolpho Lisboa Pickpocket & Phone-Snatch Ring
scams.description:
Manaus Centro Histórico — the 1890s rubber-boom colonial core including Teatro Amazonas, Largo de São Sebastião, Palácio Rio Negro, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, and Porto de Manaus — is the mandatory half-day tourist circuit and hosts a documented 2025 pickpocket and phone-snatch pattern. The structural feature: Centro is genuinely worth visiting (the opera house alone is a Manaus icon), but the daytime-only constraint is non-negotiable since walking back to a hotel after dinner draws the worst of the phone-snatch and mugging activity.

The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Teatro Amazonas square ('Largo de São Sebastião') phone-snatch — tourists take photos of the pink-and-blue opera house, a motorbike rider or pedestrian snatches the phone and runs through the adjacent calçadões; (b) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa (1883 cast-iron market, a Manaus landmark) crowded-aisle pickpocket — vendors' teams work with lookouts; during peak tourist hours (10 AM–noon and 3–5 PM) crowd-density lifts wallets + phones; (c) Porto de Manaus waterfront 'guide offer' — a 'helpful local' offers to show you the Encontro das Águas boat piers, steers you into a closed section, demands R$100 'tip'; (d) fake 'Teatro Amazonas guide R$80' on the front steps — the actual guided tour is R$20 purchased at the INSIDE ticket window (official 30-min tour in English); (e) aggressive vendor pressure at Palácio Rio Negro + Ponta Negra 'artisanal market' stalls — price-padding + bag rifling; (f) Centro-to-hotel walk at night (after 8 PM) — tourists walking back from dinner are targeted for phone-snatch + mugging on the quieter streets (Av. Eduardo Ribeiro, Rua 10 de Julho); (g) 'medical emergency' distraction at Largo de São Sebastião — older woman 'dizzy / blood pressure / call my son' while accomplice picks pocket; (h) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa 'samples' vendor pushing a piece of tambaqui fish or tucupi paste into your hand then demanding R$50.

For travelers, the practical defense is to confine Centro to daytime and keep valuables minimal. Do the Centro Histórico circuit daytime only (8 AM–5 PM, preferably 9 AM–noon when tourist police visibility is highest), Uber back to your hotel from any dinner spot, and carry only a decoy phone plus R$100 cash with passport, cards, and primary phone in the hotel safe. Teatro Amazonas photos: take quickly from the Largo de São Sebastião paving stones then stow your phone immediately — motorbike phone-snatch is documented. For the Teatro Amazonas guided tour, enter and pay R$20 at the inside ticket window (official 30-min tours in English at 9 AM, 11 AM, 2 PM, 4 PM); refuse every 'guide R$80' offer on the exterior steps. At Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, carry a cross-body bag in front and refuse every 'sample' push — if someone places food in your hand, drop it and walk away. At Porto de Manaus, stay with the main tour group; never follow a 'local guide' into a closed pier area. If you see a 'medical emergency' approach, say 'I will call 192 (SAMU)' — that exposes the scam instantly. Consider a half-day guided Centro Histórico tour via Amazonastur or Viverde at R$120–R$200 per person. DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192.
scams.avoidance: Centro Histórico DAYTIME ONLY (9 AM–noon best); Uber back from any dinner spot Decoy phone + R$100 cash only; passport + cards + main phone in hotel safe Teatro Amazonas guided tour R$20 at INSIDE ticket window (9 AM / 11 AM / 2 PM / 4 PM English) Cross-body bag in FRONT at Mercado Adolpho Lisboa; refuse every 'sample' push DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192
scams.location: Teatro Amazonas, Largo de São Sebastião, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, Porto de Manaus
scams.tldr: Manaus Centro Histórico runs documented 2025 motorbike phone-snatches at Teatro Amazonas, crowded-aisle pickpocket teams at Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, 'helpful local' guide-trap fees at Porto de Manaus, and 'medical emergency' distraction theft at Largo de São Sebastião — Centro is daytime-only territory.

scams.name: Ponta Negra & Centro Restaurant Couvert + Serviço Padding & 'Peixe do Dia' Market-Price Trap
scams.description:
Manaus dining corridors — Ponta Negra orla (the main tourist waterfront), Centro Histórico (around Teatro Amazonas and Largo de São Sebastião), and Mercado Adolpho Lisboa (the cast-iron tambaqui and tucupi market) — host the standard Brazilian tourist-restaurant overcharge pattern, with a distinctive Amazonian 'peixe do dia' (daily fish) market-price trap built around tambaqui, pirarucu, and tucunaré.

Brazilian restaurant law (Lei 13.419/2017) makes the 10% serviço charge OPTIONAL — you can refuse it, particularly for poor service. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Ponta Negra orla 'couvert artístico R$80–R$150 per person' (legitimate R$15–R$35 for a genuine Amazonian musician — boi-bumbá, carimbó, forró); (b) 'peixe do dia preço de mercado' (daily fish market price) with no R$ per kg quoted — bill arrives R$280 for a 500g tambaqui fillet (real R$100–R$180 for same quantity); (c) 'pirarucu fresco R$350 mandatory weight' arrives as 900g serving billed R$850 (fair pirarucu is R$120–R$220 per kg, portion 400–500g is R$60–R$110); (d) 'tucunaré grelhado' at Ponta Negra barracas billed as 1kg when served 600g (weigh in front of you before cooking); (e) 'serviço 10%' added silently with the menu showing 'serviço opcional' fine print; (f) credit-card surcharge 5–10% only at bill-time ('we prefer PIX'); (g) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa food-stall 'tacacá gringo price' R$35 (local R$12) + 'tucupi shot R$15' (local R$4); (h) 'caldeirada de tambaqui para dois' at Ponta Negra restaurants served as portion for one, billed R$280 (fair R$120–R$180 for a genuine 2-person portion).

For travelers, the practical defense is to confirm prices in writing before ordering. Before sitting, ask for the menu (carta) in Portuguese and photograph the page showing the couvert artístico amount, the 'serviço opcional' notice (Lei 13.419/2017 makes it optional), and any credit-card surcharge — and for Amazonian fish, agree the price per kg in writing before cooking (fair 2026: tambaqui R$100–R$180/kg, pirarucu R$120–R$220/kg, tucunaré R$80–R$150/kg). Reputable Ponta Negra: Banzeiro (Google 4.6+, Amazonian fine dining, R$120–R$280), Caxiri (riverside, R$80–R$180), Tambaqui de Banda (R$60–R$120). Reputable Centro: Peixaria do Moraes (R$70–R$160), Mercado Adolpho Lisboa upper-floor stalls (tacacá R$12–R$18 local price). Avoid English-only menus posted outside — walk 1–2 blocks inland for authentic prices. If serviço is added for poor service, politely refuse and cite Lei 13.419/2017. For Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, pay in Portuguese ('quanto é?') with small bills; if a stall quotes R$35 for tacacá, walk to the next stall — the next will be R$12. PROCON Amazonas 151 for billing disputes; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: BEFORE sitting, confirm couvert + serviço + card surcharge IN WRITING; photograph menu Fish: agree R$ per kg BEFORE cooking (tambaqui R$100–R$180/kg; pirarucu R$120–R$220/kg) Reputable: Banzeiro / Caxiri / Tambaqui de Banda (Ponta Negra); Peixaria do Moraes (Centro) REFUSE serviço if poor service (Lei 13.419/2017 — OPTIONAL); PROCON Amazonas 151 Mercado Adolpho Lisboa: pay in small bills + Portuguese; walk to next stall if gringo-priced
scams.location: Ponta Negra orla restaurants, Centro Histórico cafés, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa stalls
scams.tldr: Ponta Negra orla and Centro Histórico restaurants run R$80–R$150 'couvert artístico' (real R$15–R$35), 'peixe do dia preço de mercado' bills R$280 for 500g tambaqui (real R$100–R$180/kg), and silent serviço 10% — Brazilian Lei 13.419/2017 makes serviço optional and you can refuse it.

scams.name: Amazonas Regional Uber & Mototaxi Coordinated-Scam Pattern (Santarém / Alto do Chão Template)
scams.description:
Amazonas regional rideshare (Santarém, Alto do Chão, Parintins) has a documented 2025 coordinated Uber scam pattern that Manaus-based travelers encounter when venturing beyond the capital. The pattern is detailed in a multi-comment community thread documenting a team of drivers and passengers working together to defraud tourists via fake route detours, 'broken-meter' cash demands mid-trip, and passport-card skimming. The structural problem: Amazonas tourism extends well beyond Manaus, but rideshare oversight thins out fast outside the capital.

The 2025 Santarém / Alto do Chão pattern (translatable to Manaus regional Uber and side-trips): (a) coordinated driver-passenger team — you book Uber, the app shows a driver 5 min away; en route to pickup, a passenger (planted accomplice) is already in the car; at pickup the driver claims 'another ride ahead of you' and asks you to wait or share — accomplice-passenger engages you in conversation while driver takes a 'shortcut' detour padding the fare; (b) 'meter / app failed — R$100 cash' demand mid-trip; (c) driver asking to 'see your card to confirm the Uber payment' — card skimming via hidden reader; (d) driver taking a deliberately long route to pad the in-app fare (Uber Brazil allows surge + long-route charges); (e) destination 'changed' — driver claims 'your hotel is closed' or 'that area is dangerous, I'll take you to a better hotel' — steering you to a commissioned 'safe' hotel that charges 3x normal rate; (f) in Parintins during Boi-Bumbá festival (June), rideshare supply collapses — unlicensed mototaxis + private-car drivers emerge charging 5–10x normal with robbery risk; (g) Alto do Chão river-beach day-trip: 'driver package R$600 round-trip + waiting' offered by airport tout — real Uber R$150–R$250 round-trip + hold on driver with hourly wait rate via in-app.

For travelers, the practical defense lives in driver-match verification and refusing card-handovers. Always verify the driver's name, plate, and photo match the in-app profile before entering, and never hand your credit or debit card to any driver — payment is only via the in-app card or cash at end of trip — refusing every 'let me scan your card to confirm payment' demand. Don't share an Uber with an already-present 'other passenger' unless you explicitly booked UberPool; if a stranger is in the car on pickup, cancel and report via the safety button. Follow the route on your phone's GPS (Google Maps in split-screen with Uber) — if the driver deviates significantly, ask 'está certo o caminho?' and if suspicious, ask to stop at the next public place (mall, hotel) and cancel/rebook. Refuse every mid-trip 'meter broke, R$100 cash' demand — Uber Brazil uses GPS, not a meter; the in-app price is final. If a driver claims 'your hotel is closed / dangerous,' insist on the original address or stop at the nearest public place — never let a stranger redirect your destination. For Parintins Festival de Boi-Bumbá (late June), book transfers 3–6 months ahead via reputable operators. For Alto do Chão day-trip, book Uber round-trip with driver wait (in-app 'Hora por hora' at R$40–R$60/hour) for typical R$400–R$550 total. DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190; Uber in-app 24/7 safety line.
scams.avoidance: VERIFY driver name + plate + photo MATCH app BEFORE entering; cancel if mismatched NEVER share Uber with 'other passenger'; NEVER hand card to driver for any reason Follow GPS route on your phone; if deviation, demand stop at public place + cancel REFUSE every 'meter broke R$100 cash' mid-trip demand (Uber uses in-app GPS pricing) Book Parintins / Alto do Chão transfers via reputable operators 3–6 mo ahead; DEATUR +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Manaus Uber pickups + regional Amazonas Uber (Santarém, Alto do Chão, Parintins)
scams.tldr: Amazonas regional Uber (Santarém, Alto do Chão, Parintins) runs coordinated driver-passenger teams with fake route detours, 'broken-meter' R$100 cash demands mid-trip, and 'let me see your card to confirm payment' skimming — Parintins Boi-Bumbá Festival sees rideshare collapse and unlicensed-mototaxi robbery risk.
